PullRequest.Title: Modern UI: Fix compact status bar item spacing
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes the compact-density status bar gaps reported in #334933 while preserving the established spacing of ordinary status bar items. The change restores the semantic margin exceptions for joined and colored items and adds production-component fixture coverage.

Fixes #334933

## What was broken

Modern UI's compact-density rule reapplied a 2px margin to every status bar label. That overrode the status bar's narrower semantic rules:

- joined split-button edges reopened into a visible gap;
- colored labels no longer covered their complete item background;
- middle segments of three-part controls could gain unintended spacing.

## What changed

- Restore zero margins only on joined and colored edges in compact density.
- Preserve the existing compact spacing for ordinary items.
- Add a computed-style regression matrix for default and compact density.
- Add real `StatusbarEntryItem` fixtures for simple, colored, two-part split, three-part split, and colored split controls.
- Exercise Dark, Light, and Dark High Contrast themes using production status bar heights and platform typography.

## Visual audit

**Result: 6/6 density and theme variants pass.**

The fixture captures below use the production `StatusbarEntryItem`, production CSS, the macOS workbench system font, and identical dimensions and zoom.

### Simple button — matched before and after

![Simple status bar button before and after in default and compact density](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e97a3d1f-be75-4f72-b5bb-5818f0b4ca89)

The simple button is intentionally unchanged: default density retains 3px margins and compact density retains 2px margins.

### Branch + sync split button — matched before and after

![Branch and sync split status bar button before and after in default and compact density](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40d40b2e-2384-4092-81fe-13fcdafd41e1)

Default density remains unchanged. In compact density, the pre-fix 4px visual gap closes to a 0px seam while the outer compact spacing remains intact.

## Coverage matrix

| Area | Scenarios | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary items | Simple text, icon + text, hovered fill | Existing spacing preserved |
| Colored items | Warning, error, remote, colored split | 0/0px label-to-item insets |
| Two-part split | Branch + sync, primary + dropdown | 0px joined seam |
| Three-part split | Left, middle, and right segments | 0px at both seams |
| Density | Default and compact | 2/2 |
| Theme | Dark, Light, Dark High Contrast | 3/3 |

The `Screenshots & Tests` report provides the complete fixture theme sweep.

## Testing

1. Enable `workbench.experimental.modernUI`.
2. In default density, hover ordinary, colored, and joined status bar items and verify the existing spacing is unchanged.
3. Switch `window.density.layout` to `compact`.
4. Verify ordinary controls retain compact spacing.
5. Verify branch + sync and other split controls have no gap at joined edges.
6. Verify colored hover surfaces cover their complete item backgrounds.

Validation completed locally:

- `npm run transpile-client`
- Modern UI browser unit suite: **82 passing**
- ESLint on the changed TypeScript files
- Stylelint on the changed CSS
- Component Explorer render/dispose sweep: **14/14 variants passed**
- Code OSS Dev 1.141.0 on macOS arm64 in isolated default- and compact-density profiles

The local ffmpeg build lacks the `drawtext` filter, so the raw scenario videos could not be captioned; screenshots and independent DOM geometry assertions are unaffected.

Scenarios.Scenario: Compact-density status bar rendering and updates in the workbench
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The browser matches two additional selectors during normal style resolution for status-bar labels. Density changes or status-item DOM/class updates can trigger style recalculation, but the diff adds no script, geometry read, layout loop, or boundary call that must complete before interaction.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with the number of status-bar item labels in one workbench window, realistically tens of elements. The selectors are tightly scoped by the modern UI, compact-density, status-bar, direct-child, and class predicates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser style matching/layout remains handled by the existing rendering pipeline; the diff introduces no task fan-out, queue, mutex, or parallel operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved. Browser selector/style caches may be invalidated by the same existing DOM or class changes as before; the diff adds only two declarations to those recalculations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the changed mechanism: two scoped CSS selectors add bounded style-matching work and alter margins only; no transitive expensive boundary is reached.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact selector-matching time is browser-dependent, but the effective element count and lack of synchronous layout reads or repeated JavaScript work make a user-visible regression implausible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The production change adds negligible bounded CSS matching work and fixes layout without introducing repeated layout measurement, retained state, or expensive I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Modern UI browser unit test for density-dependent margins
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new test synchronously creates one item at a time and calls getComputedStyle before asserting results. Fourteen measurements must finish for this single test, but this path is test-only and not part of workbench startup or interaction.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed matrix of seven status-item class scenarios across two densities, for 14 create/measure/remove cycles.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All fourteen DOM/style measurements run serially in one test invocation; there is no concurrency or burst across resources.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No explicit cache or miss behavior. Browser style data may be reused internally, while each getComputedStyle can synchronously ensure styles are current for a tiny DOM.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that getComputedStyle introduces synchronous style work, and equally high confidence that it is bounded to 14 test-only calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Individual style-resolution duration varies by test browser, but cardinality is fixed and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The finite regression matrix adds trivial test-suite work and cannot affect product runtime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Component Explorer rendering and CI screenshot coverage for status-bar fixtures
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Selecting a fixture creates editor services, DOM rows, and production StatusbarEntryItem instances before that fixture is ready for capture. A blocking CI sweep covers six themed default/compact variants; comparison fixtures are non-blocking explorer fixtures. This work is isolated to the component-fixture test bundle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Headless visual fixture capture performed by the existing Component Explorer screenshot harness after each blocking fixture renders
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six blocking captures: default and compact density across dark, light, and dark-high-contrast themes. A full explorer render of all defined variants would construct 114 status-bar entries, but fixtures are mounted by variant rather than all by this module itself.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No status-bar fixture group or corresponding status-bar screenshot captures existed before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fixture DOM/service construction must finish before each corresponding screenshot can be captured; this affects only visual-test/explorer execution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Blocking sweep constructs 15 entries per variant across six variants, totaling 90 StatusbarEntryItem instances; all defined variants total 114 instances if each is rendered once. Counts are static constants, not user-input or repository-size dependent.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each fixture's scenarios and entries are constructed synchronously. The fixture utility notes explorer UI may render multiple selected fixtures in parallel, while the configured worktree screenshot runner has maxSlots 1; the diff adds no independent concurrency or unbounded Promise fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache or remote lookup is used. Module definitions register fixture variants once in the test bundle; each mounted variant creates fresh services and items and registers every item with the fixture disposable store for teardown.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff adds bounded test rendering and six blocking visual captures; fixture code contains no network, filesystem, IPC, database, or subprocess call, and created StatusbarEntryItem objects are owned by the disposable store.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Harness capture duration is environment-dependent, but the number of new captures and DOM objects is fixed and modest.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added CI/explorer work is intentional, fixed-cardinality coverage with explicit disposal, not unbounded eager product work or a realistic throughput failure.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and every diff page. The only production effect is two highly scoped CSS selectors; the remaining changes are bounded unit-test, fixture, and screenshot documentation additions. No actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
